newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on short-covering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended on Wednesday a shade up from its previous New York close after short-covering and some Swiss buying, bullion dealers said.

"There was some short-covering during the day and the Swiss started buying in the early afternoon," said one bullion dealer. Bullion ended at US$353.40/90 an ounce Wednesday against New York's US$353.30/80 close on Tuesday.

Hong Kong traders said they were watching the current critical level of $354 per ounce, and if that resistence was not breached in New York tonight, the price would sink back down to between $347-350 per ounce.

"People were encouraged by the rebound in New York on Friday, but they're not quite convinced," said one gold source. Physical demand had slowed down on the price increase, and because the peak season had ended, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$13 higher at HK$3,272 a tael.
The carry over charge per ten taels at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -4.00 from its previous fix at nil.
